subject: Urgent: production spikes and failed streams — suspected SDK header-splitting causing retries
messages:
From: Tim Carter <tim.carter@skybound.io>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: (Urgent) production spikes and failed streams

Priyom —

We started seeing a sharp rise in 5xx errors and severe throughput degradation across our ingestion pipelines this morning (~08:50 PST). Error rates jump from 0.2% to ~7% and sustained request latency increases by ~450ms p95. Our SREs traced the issue to repeated client SDK retries originating from long-lived streaming connections that appear to be failing mid-response.

Attached is a short log excerpt (sdk_log_excerpt.txt) and a pcap. In the logs you can see the client reporting "invalid stream frame" errors followed by automated retry storms. We're on Redwood SDK v1.2.4 (default streaming mode).

This is impacting our customer dashboards and some critical SLA checks. Can we get an immediate triage and a mitigation? We are prepared to open a call — please advise next steps.

Thanks,
Tim
Tim Carter
Head of SRE, Skybound Analytics
phone: +1-415-555-0192

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Tim Carter <tim.carter@skybound.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:28:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: (Urgent) production spikes and failed streams

Tim — thanks for the heads up and for sending the artifacts. I'm escalating to engineering and will coordinate an immediate triage.

Initial asks:
- Marissa / Vivek — can you take a look at the logs/pcap and confirm whether this aligns with any known parser edge cases?
- Tim — do you have a short window (15–30 minutes) for a quick screen-share? If not, we'll start async.

Immediate mitigation we can try while investigating: disable SDK auto-retries for streaming clients and fall back to short polling for the most critical routes. Can we toggle that server-side for a portion of traffic?

I will keep you updated every 30 minutes until we have a root cause.

— Priyom
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Tim Carter <tim.carter@skybound.io>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 10:07:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: (Urgent) production spikes and failed streams

Thanks Tim and Priyom — I've pulled the pcap and the log snippet. High-level triage:

- The client logs show repeated occurrences of "header-splitting" errors in the streaming parser; frames are being interpreted as separate header blocks mid-stream.
- Packet capture shows intermediaries fragmenting frames in a way that, combined with the SDK's current HTTP/2 streaming parser behavior (v1.2.4), can lead to spurious "end-of-headers" detection.
- When the SDK triggers a local parse error it performs exponential retries on the stream which can cascade into increased load and timeouts on our routing nodes.

Immediate recommended mitigations (short term):
1) Disable client-side auto-retries for streaming on Skybound's production clients (we can provide a feature flag).
2) If possible, temporarily pin to SDK v1.2.3 which does not include the new streaming parser optimizations introduced in 1.2.4.
3) Server-side: apply a short-lived heuristic to drop obvious mid-frame header boundaries (we can push a canary rule to the edge).

Longer term: engineering will propose a parser hardening patch and an SDK patch to properly coalesce fragmented frames and avoid retries on parser recoverable errors. We'll open a dedicated ticket and provide an ETA within 48 hours.

Tim — do you want an immediate emergency call? If not, we'll proceed with the mitigations above and confirm behavior.

— Marissa
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Tim Carter <tim.carter@skybound.io>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 11:52:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: (Urgent) production spikes and failed streams

Update from infra: we've prepared a two-phase response.

Phase A (hours):
- Push canary rule at edge to be more tolerant of fragmented header boundaries for streams coming from Skybound IP ranges.
- Provide a temporary feature flag to Skybound to disable streaming auto-retries (small config change on their side).

Phase B (days):
- Implement SDK patch (v1.2.5-beta) that coalesces fragmented frames and treats mid-frame header tokens as recoverable. We'll run unit tests and a gated canary across internal services before recommending a customer upgrade.

Business ask: Skybound is requesting an SLA credit due to the incident. Naomi, can you advise on the standard process to approve a one-off credit pending postmortem? Priyom, please capture the customer's requested credit amount (they'll send a form).

I'll start the edge canary this afternoon and coordinate with Ops to monitor load.

— Vivek
VP, Infrastructure Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Tim Carter <tim.carter@skybound.io>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:43:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: (Urgent) production spikes and failed streams

Thanks all — the mitigations look good. We applied the no-retry flag for a portion of traffic and saw error rates fall back to baseline within ~30 minutes. Canary edge rule also reduced the timeout cascades.

We have completed initial impact assessment and submitted the SLA credit request form (sla_credit_request_form.pdf). We'd like a short RCA and the timeline for SDK v1.2.5 release and a recommended upgrade window.

Next steps requested from Redwood:
- RCA document (high level) within 48 business hours.
- Timeline for SDK patch and canary plan (ETA for 1.2.5 stable).
- Confirmation on whether Redwood will provide a one-time credit for the incident while we finalize the postmortem.

Appreciate the quick response — the incident hit a subset of our customers and we need the RCA for our internal ops review.

— Tim
Head of SRE, Skybound Analytics
